Initial (parametric) spatial triggering-function guess

Source: R/trigger.R
trigger_spatial_init.Rd

Builds the Loop-0 isotropic spatial triggering kernel \(g(x,y) = 1 / (x^2/\text{scale}^2 + y^2/\text{scale}^2 + \epsilon)\) on a regular grid, normalized to integrate to 1 via simpson.2D().

Usage

trigger_spatial_init(
  x_range = 1000,
  y_range = x_range,
  x_step = 200,
  y_step = x_step,
  scale = 40000,
  epsilon = 0.01
)

Arguments

x_range, y_range

Half-width of the grid along x/y (grid spans [-range, range]), in the linear units of the working CRS (metres for a UTM projection); default 1000 for both, i.e. a +/-1 km window. This is how far from an event the triggering kernel can reach, so choose it with care: see Choosing the triggering reach in fit_semihawkes().

x_step, y_step

Grid step along x/y, in the linear units of the working CRS (metres for a UTM projection); default 200 for both, i.e. 200 m. x_range / x_step and y_range / y_step must be whole numbers (5 for the defaults), so that each grid is centred on 0 and has the odd number of points simpson.2D() needs.

scale, epsilon

Kernel shape parameters: \(g(x,y) = 1 / (x^2/\text{scale}^2 + y^2/\text{scale}^2 + \epsilon)\). Defaults (40000, 0.01) match the original script.

Value

A list of class "semihawkes_trigger_spatial" with x, y (grid coordinate sequences), basevalue (length(x) x length(y) matrix, normalized), and fun (a function fun(x, y) that bilinearly interpolates via fields::interp.surface(), returning 0 – not NA – outside the grid, matching the original excite.spatial.fun).

Examples

h <- trigger_spatial_init(x_range = 2000, x_step = 100)
h
#> <semihawkes_trigger_spatial>
#>   41 x 41 grid, x in [-2000, 2000], y in [-2000, 2000]
image(h$x, h$y, h$basevalue, asp = 1,
      xlab = "x offset (m)", ylab = "y offset (m)")
